req.title: Accept comma-separated status codes
req.statement: The system shall select one code at random when /status/<code> is called with a comma-separated list.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /status/<codes> with a comma-separated list shall select one code at random. Tests must verify: (1) positive — a valid comma-separated list returns one of the listed codes; (2) negative — an invalid code in the list returns 400; (3) boundary — a single-item list (no comma) returns exactly that code; (4) weighted choices are parsed correctly; (5) the random selection covers all listed codes over many trials. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes, checking both sides of the comma-detection branch, and verifying the set of possible outcomes exactly.

tests.name: test_comma_separated_returns_one_of_listed_codes
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Assert response status code is exactly one of {200, 301, 404}
expected: Response status code is a member of the set {200, 301, 404}
No other status code is returned
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_comma_separated_returns_one_of_listed_codes():
    allowed = {200, 301, 404}
    seen = set()
    for _ in range(60):
        r = client.get('/status/200,301,404', follow_redirects=False)
        assert r.status_code in allowed, f"Unexpected status: {r.status_code}"
        seen.add(r.status_code)
    # Over 60 trials all three codes should appear (probabilistic but robust)
    assert seen == allowed, f"Not all codes seen: {seen}"

test_comma_separated_returns_one_of_listed_codes()

tests.name: test_invalid_code_in_comma_list_returns_400
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Assert response status code is exactly 400
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_invalid_code_in_comma_list_returns_400():
    r = client.get('/status/200,abc,404', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 400, f"Expected 400, got {r.status_code}"
    assert b'Invalid status code' in r.data, f"Unexpected body: {r.data}"

test_invalid_code_in_comma_list_returns_400()

tests.name: test_two_code_comma_list_returns_only_those_two
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Assert each response is exactly 200 or 500
Assert both codes appear at least once
expected: Only status codes 200 and 500 are returned
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_two_code_comma_list_returns_only_those_two():
    allowed = {200, 500}
    seen = set()
    for _ in range(50):
        r = client.get('/status/200,500', follow_redirects=False)
        assert r.status_code in allowed, f"Unexpected status: {r.status_code}"
        seen.add(r.status_code)
    assert seen == allowed, f"Not all codes seen: {seen}"

test_two_code_comma_list_returns_only_those_two()

def test_invalid_weight_in_comma_list_returns_400():

actions: Send GET /status/200,200 (comma present but both codes identical)
Assert response status code is exactly 200 every time
expected: Response status code is exactly 200 on every request
The comma branch is taken (comma is present) but result is deterministic

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_comma_list_with_two_identical_codes_returns_that_code():
    for _ in range(10):
        r = client.get('/status/200,200', follow_redirects=False)
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"Expected 200, got {r.status_code}"
